One Childhood. Many Opportunities.
Welcome to Eton End School
A warm and welcoming Prep school in Datchet, where every child is known and supported to thrive. With a strong focus on academic excellence, pastoral care and personal development, the school nurtures confident, curious learners in a caring community that prepares them well for the next stage of their education.
Pre-Prep
Excellence Backed by a Legacy of Learning
As a part of the Inspired Learning Group, Eton End School draws from the collective strength of 25 schools across the UK. This gives our students access to a wider network, richer resources, and innovative learning pathways.
35 Eton Rd, Datchet, Slough SL3 9AX, United Kingdom
©2026 Eton End. All rights reserved.
Parent Portal

Curriculum
At Eton End, our curriculum is designed to be both enriching and creative, inspiring pupils to explore, discover, and develop their talents across a wide range of subjects.
Academic excellence is complemented by opportunities in Art, Music, Drama, and Sport, allowing children to grow as confident, well-rounded individuals. Learning is engaging and hands-on, with a focus on curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving, ensuring that pupils not only acquire knowledge but also the skills to apply it creatively. From the classroom to the outdoors, and through specialist teaching and exciting enrichment activities, our curriculum encourages every child to thrive, fostering a lifelong love of learning.
During these sessions, pupils receive tailored support and challenge, whether that’s reinforcing key skills, exploring areas of personal interest, or extending their learning beyond the curriculum. This dedicated time allows teachers to work closely with each child, ensuring learning is purposeful, engaging, and suited to their unique needs and abilities. It’s a valued part of our week that helps every pupil make excellent progress and take ownership of their learning journey.
At our school, we are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and nurturing environment where every child is supported to reach their full potential. Our Special Educational Needs (SEN) provision begins with the early identification of individual needs, followed by support that reflects each pupil’s strengths and challenges. Our staff receive ongoing training to deliver differentiated teaching, ensuring that learning is accessible and engaging for all. We work in close partnership with parents, teaching assistants, and external specialists when required, to provide effective interventions, including small group sessions and targeted one-to-one support. Our caring, community-focused ethos ensures that every child feels valued, included, and empowered to succeed.
At Eton End, we are proud to nurture and challenge our gifted and talented children through a rich, stimulating curriculum and personal learning that encourages curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking.
Our teachers provide carefully differentiated learning experiences, ensuring each child is stretched and inspired to reach their full potential. Opportunities for extension are woven throughout the school day from problem-solving challenges and higher-level questioning in lessons, to enrichment clubs, specialist workshops, and leadership roles that develop confidence and independence. We celebrate excellence while fostering a lifelong love of learning and discovery.

Pre Prep
Incorporating Reception, Year 1 and 2, Pre Prep is where our children begin their formal learning journey.
We ensure all children are offered rich, challenging and fun experiences in a secure and friendly environment. To keep learning exciting, a series of topic-based approaches is used. By linking separate subjects under the umbrella of a topic, the learning is fun and stimulating.
As pupils progress, lessons become more subject-focused, supported by high-quality enrichment activities. The curriculum is skills-based and knowledge-supported, providing a strong foundation for future learning. Specialist lessons are introduced early: from Reception, children enjoy Spanish, Music, Digital and Physical Education; Year 1 adds swimming at the Eton College pool. This measured approach allows pupils to benefit from both form-based learning and specialist expertise.
Qualified teachers, small class sizes, and generous teaching assistant support enable us to provide the best education for every child—from those needing extra support to those with exceptional talents. Staff know pupils well and inspire them to live by the school motto: “I am, I can, I ought, I will.”
Learning at Eton End motivates children to grow in confidence and become independent learners and thinkers. We place equal importance on emotional literacy and academic success, ensuring pupils feel valued and safe. Effective pastoral arrangements, a focus on growth mindset, and thoughtful assessment support each child’s progress. Pupils are encouraged to take responsibility from an early age—through opportunities such as the School Council—and celebrate both their own achievements and those of their peers.

Prep School
At Eton End, we take pride in offering a broad and enriching Prep School curriculum that nurtures pupils’ strengths across a wide range of subjects, both inside and outside the classroom.
Rigorous and inspiring academic teaching is complemented by creative and physical subjects—including Art, Music, Sport, and Drama—ensuring every child receives a well-rounded education.
Our pupils learn in a happy, secure environment where they are valued and respected as individuals. We encourage them to develop lively, enquiring minds, fostering curiosity and discussion rather than passive acceptance.
The school’s Form Tutor Model supports strong academic, pastoral, and social development throughout Prep. Pupils are taught by specialist teachers in Sport, Music, Digital and Languages, with Years 5 and 6 benefiting from specialist Science lessons. At this stage, competitive sport becomes a key feature, with matches and tournaments against other schools providing exciting opportunities for teamwork and achievement. Pupils can also join musical ensembles, from Junior and Senior Choirs to instrumental groups, further enhancing their creative development.
Our education is broad, balanced, and inspiring, helping pupils discover their full range of talents and skills. They acquire knowledge and understanding of the world around them, equipping them for future challenges. Prep at Eton End also prepares pupils for 11+, Common Entrance, or Scholarship examinations, providing a strong foundation for progression to a wide range of senior schools and local grammar schools.

Part of ILG
Our school is part of the Inspired Learning Group (‘ILG’) of independent schools and nurseries.
Our Aim
ILG strives to create safe and inspiring educational environments where children can grow into positive and impactful members of society who will, one day in turn, shape the outlook of the next generation. Our schools and nurseries combine traditional values and forward-thinking ideas to help every single pupil realise their potential, so they are prepared to take on jobs that have not yet been invented.
Our Philosophy
ILG believes, first and foremost, in putting your child at the heart of everything we do. We endeavour to provide educational excellence within a culture of care to nurture each pupil the best we can. We want to offer a wide range of opportunities, both academic and extra-curricular, so that all our children are endowed with the spirit to aspire and become twenty first century citizens.

Pastoral Care & Wellbeing
At Eton End, we are proud of our nurturing and supportive ethos, where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to thrive as an individual. We believe children learn best when they feel happy, safe, and respected, and when they know they are treated fairly. Our small class sizes and strong pastoral care enable us to build trusting, empathetic relationships between pupils, staff, and parents.
Each child is supported first and foremost by their Form Teacher, who plays a central role in their daily life at school. The Form Teacher provides continuity of care, getting to know each pupil closely and acting as a first point of contact for both the child and their parents. Working alongside them is our dedicated Pastoral Care Team, led by Miss Logan, Deputy Head (Pastoral), who oversees the wellbeing of every pupil across the school. Together, this team ensures that each child receives the right balance of guidance, encouragement, and support throughout their Eton End journey.
Kindness and respect are central to life at Eton End. From an early age, pupils learn to care for one another and to celebrate differences. Our House system—Ash, Beech, Elm, and Oak—brings children of all ages together, fostering teamwork, collaboration, and a healthy sense of competition through a wide range of inter-house activities.
Pastoral Care and Citizenship are woven into every aspect of school life, helping pupils develop spiritually, morally, socially, and culturally. We aim to prepare every child for the opportunities and responsibilities of the wider world, including a strong understanding of Fundamental British Values.

“The Nest” Nursery at Eton End
Where little steps lead to big dreams
At Eton End Nursery, we provide a caring and joyful environment where every child feels safe, valued, and inspired to learn. Through play, exploration, and creative activities, children build confidence and curiosity from an early age. Our experienced staff nurture each child’s individual journey, helping them grow in independence and joy. With the addition of our new Baby Room, even our youngest learners can now begin their Eton End journey in a calm, supportive space designed just for them.
The Nest and EYFS at Eton End
At the heart of Eton End, our early years provision, from The Nest Nursery through the EYFS, offers a warm, nurturing environment where children thrive, explore, and develop a lifelong love of learning. In The Nest, babies and toddlers from 3 months old enjoy a safe and stimulating setting with play-based activities, imaginative experiences, and weekly PE, Music, and Spanish lessons. Flexible term-time and full-time options, as well as 15- and 30-hour government-funded childcare, ensure families have the support and continuity they need.
As children move into the EYFS, learning becomes a joyful blend of structured activities and play, designed to spark curiosity, creativity, and confidence. Children develop key skills in literacy, numeracy, problem-solving, and social interaction, while exploring the world through hands-on experiences, creative arts, and outdoor adventures. Every day encourages them to ask questions, try new things, and grow in a supportive, inclusive environment where their individuality is celebrated.
We value open and consistent communication between home and school, ensuring parents are fully involved in their child’s learning journey. Outdoor activity is just as important as classroom-based learning, and our children enjoy the space to explore, discover, and develop physically and socially. Educational visits and in-house parent activities further enrich their experiences and broaden learning opportunities.
Staff-to-child ratios ensure individualised attention.
